title: 2026-11-05_WHIRLPOOL_Malware_Investigation_e7d
description: Investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) device in your network has been compromised by the WHIRLPOOL malware, specifically the Linux/WhirlPool.A variant. This malware is known to establish a reverse shell, allowing unauthorized access to the system. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `target` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `target` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
```bash
ssh cyrano@target
```
2. List all services to identify the suspicious one:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services that might be related to network communication or data collection.
4. The flag is the name of the suspicious service: `ssld.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list only running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the service descriptions for any unusual or unfamiliar entries.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to network communication or data collection.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Identify the suspicious service from the previous task.
2. Inspect the service configuration to find the port it is using:
```bash
systemctl cat <service>
```
3. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration, which specifies the command launched by the service with a port number as an argument.
4. The flag is the port number used by the suspicious service: `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service>` to check the status and configuration of the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration to find the port number.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports and identify the one used by the suspicious service.

levels.title: Identify Data Collection Service
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services, including timers, to identify the one responsible for data collection:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timers that might be related to data collection.
3. Inspect the timer configuration to understand its behavior:
```bash
systemctl cat <timer>
```
4. The flag is the name of the suspicious timer: `local-inventory.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-unit-files --type=timer` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the timer configuration for any unusual or unfamiliar entries.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that might be related to data collection or system information gathering.
